findings.problem: SampleWorkflow uses raw booleans (is_validated, is_sent) and a String status instead of an enum-based typestate. Any combination of these fields represents an illegal state (e.g., is_sent=false with status="sent", or is_validated=true with status="draft").
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct and mutate the struct into logically inconsistent states. The mark_sent function does not check that the workflow is actually in a valid pre-sent state before mutating.
findings.fix: Replace the three fields (status, is_validated, is_sent) with a single WorklfowState enum that encodes allowed transitions. Remove public mutable fields; expose behavior through methods on the typestate.

findings.problem: status is a raw String. The hardening checklist requires status strings to be enums. mark_sent blindly overwrites status to "sent" without any state check.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid status values (e.g., "cancelled", "sent", "sent", "sent") can be set by any caller or mutation path. The string carries no semantics — it is just mutable text.
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with pub state: WorkflowState enum. Each variant (Draft, Validated, Sent) is an enum arm, not a string literal. mark_sent becomes a method on the pre-sent variant that returns the next variant.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are lifecycle booleans. The SKILL.md explicitly states: 'Replace lifecycle booleans with typestate transitions. Put optional lifecycle data inside the enum variant that owns it.'
findings.failure_mode: Two booleans create 4 possible combinations, only some of which are valid. Boolean fields are independently mutable, so any combination can be reached. There is no transition ordering or guard.
findings.fix: Remove both booleans. Replace with a single WorkflowState enum whose variants encode the lifecycle phase. Attach optional data (sent_at_epoch_ms) to the variant that owns it.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> living outside the lifecycle state. It can be Some with is_sent=false, or None with is_sent=true, creating logically inconsistent states.
findings.failure_mode: The optional field is decoupled from the lifecycle flags it semantically belongs to. A workflow can appear sent (is_sent=true) without a timestamp, or have a timestamp without being marked sent.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the WorkflowState enum as the payload of the Sent variant, e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. The Option is eliminated — presence of the Sent variant means the timestamp is required and present.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain semantics, validation, or newtype wrapper. The hardening checklist requires IDs carrying rules to use newtypes.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicate IDs, or non-UUID format strings are accepted without any constraint. The domain has no way to distinguish a valid workflow ID from any other string.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype, e.g. pub struct WorkflowId(String) or pub struct WorkflowId(Uuid), with a smart constructor that validates the format and returns a typed error on invalid input.

findings.problem: There is no parse boundary in this crate. Raw primitives (String for id, String for status, raw bools) are exposed as public struct fields. No smart constructors, no fallible parsing, no parse-don't-validate. Raw primitives cross the boundary without validation so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Every caller can fabricate a SampleWorkflow with any string values, any boolean combinations, and any option state. The domain core receives untrusted, unvalidated primitives instead of guaranteed-valid domain types.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated parsing module that accepts raw primitives at the shell boundary, validates them with fallible smart constructors, and produces a single trusted domain type (e.g. Workflow { id: WorkflowId, state: WorkflowState }). The enum-based WorkflowState subsumes status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms into a single type that makes illegal states unrepresentable.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists. The SKILL.md requires performance claims to be backed by workload, target hardware, baseline, new number, variance, threshold, and profiler/benchmark evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Without evidence, there is no way to verify that mark_sent's .to_string() allocation, the struct's String fields, or any hot-path behavior is within acceptable bounds.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark module measuring mark_sent allocation behavior and struct construction cost. Report heap allocations with a profiler. Without claims to justify measurement, this is a gap, not a blocker.

findings.problem: No clippy, miri, or cargo-check evidence is present. The SKILL.md requires canonical gate or fallback strict source gate (fmt, check, clippy with strict warnings, test compilation).
findings.failure_mode: Undetected warnings, potential index-slicing or arithmetic-side-effect issues, and must-use violations are not verified by any static analysis.
findings.fix: Run cargo clippy with -D warnings and all strict deny gates. Report results as evidence.

findings.problem: The mark_sent function uses .to_string() which performs a heap allocation on every call. For a performance-sensitive path this is unbounded allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated calls to mark_sent cause repeated heap allocations that cannot be budgeted or bounded. In mission-critical paths this violates the allocation discipline rule.
findings.fix: Store a &'static str for the status string in the enum variant, or compute it lazily only when formatting. Better: since the state is now an enum, status is no longer a separate String field — each variant carries a named state with zero allocation.

missing_evidence: no benchmark or profiler evidence for mark_sent allocation behavior
no miri or safety analysis evidence
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no bounded allocation anywhere)
no second-ring evidence (no CI, no measured baseline, no hardware target)
residual_risk: Typestate and domain-model violations are structural. The crate allows constructing any combination of status String, lifecycle bools, and optional timestamp — all illegal states are representable. This is the highest-severity class of defect: it undermines all downstream invariants. Without the six typestate/parse-boundary fixes, no amount of testing or linting can guarantee correctness. The crate compiles and the struct fields are trivially mutable, so the code is functionally deliverable but semantically broken.
